current_episode.title: Disability Tech and the Power of Inclusive Investing with Brittany and Rich Palmer

guest.entreprise_secondaire: Perkins School for the Blind Innovation Center
guest.bio_context: Brittany Palmer was born with a bilateral below elbow limb difference and grew up adapting to her environment without modern digital resources. She transitioned from environmental health and safety consulting to founding a disability tech company focused on equal access to travel for people with limited mobility. She now co-leads Adaptation Ventures, a pre-seed fund and investor community focused on disability, neurodivergence, accessibility, and aging.

context.real_quote: We designed for the kind of hardest user in mind, and when it hits universal appeal, it just explodes.
key_stats: Only 1% of venture capital currently goes to disability-related solutions
Founders with disabilities are 400 times less likely to raise funding than able-bodied counterparts (UK study)
Adaptation Ventures targets 20 to 30 companies across the investment period
Fund size: $150 to $250 million with 20% reserve
LP minimum: $36,000 over three years ($12,000 per year)
Portfolio company pre-seed example: $2 million in pipeline with $800,000 in deposits
Rich Palmer has been an angel investor for approximately 7 years (since 2019)
In 2020, there were no VCs in the disability tech space; by time of episode, five or six exist
entities: Perkins School for the Blind Innovation Center
